newsitem.title: USA: TWA outlines steps for recovery.
newsitem.headline: TWA outlines steps for recovery.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc said on Thursday it was taking steps to turn around its operations, including the elimination of unprofitable domestic and international routes, such as those to Athens, Frankfurt, Denver, Dallas, Houston and Phoenix.

"We believe we have made the decisions needed to address the problems of 1996. We will continue to make and implement these decisions in the months ahead," TWA Chief Executive Gerald Gitner said at the annual shareholders meeting.
The airline will also attempt to increase the number of passengers traveling through its St. Louis hub, he said.
"We will build up trans-Atlantic flying from St. Louis not as a replacement for JFK flying, but as a supplement to JFK," Gitner said, referring to New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport.

The carrier is also increasing its advertising in the New York City area to boost traffic through JFK and is making an undisclosed investment into customer service facilities at that airport, he said.
"More than 90 percent of our non-aircraft capital spending this year will be devoted to JFK facilities improvements," Gitner said.

TWA also is trying to attract more business passengers and will announce additional travel enhancements this summer, he said. "The bottom line should be a significant increase in yield resulting from more business travelers and an improved fare mix," Gitner said.

TWA ranked second in on-time flight arrivals, according to a government report scheduled to be released next week. Gitner preempted the U.S. Department of Transportation's announcement of the arrival statistics by releasing the figure during the annual meeting.

In April, TWA reported its 1997 first-quarter loss widened to $71.6 million, or $1.54 a share, from a loss of $37.1 million, or $1.46, in the same period the previous year. Revenues fell to $762.3 million from $782.4 million.
